in_hebrew.name: עזבאג
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The name Hawk is derived from the Hebrew word 'עזבאג' (Azavag), which means 'hawk' or 'falcon'. The Hebrew language has a rich history and is considered the foundation of the Western European languages, including English.

in_greek.name: αετος
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Hawk in Greek is derived from the word 'αετος' (aetos), which can mean 'eagle' or 'hawk'. The Greek language has a significant influence on the development of the Western European languages, including English, and has been used in the Bible for various names and expressions.

in_latin.name: Hierax
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Hawk in Latin is 'Hierax'. The Latin language, being the language of the ancient Romans, has a deep connection to the Judeo-Christian tradition and has influenced the naming conventions in Western Europe and beyond. The name Hierax, derived from the Greek word 'αετος' (aetos), meaning 'hawk', has been used in various contexts in Latin literature and inscriptions.
